what_happened: The person running Athena saw that since 12:00 UTC on 10 Nov five jobs were rejected because the cause they set out to fix was not supported by the records. The acceptance-point check failed twice. "Show cited jobs' files to the reader" was already done. "Resolve every cited job to its reading" rested on a cause the records contradict. "Print deliverable counts for carried jobs" rested on a false fact. The error review of one rejected job queued the next two requests, so each rejection led to another request built on the same wrong premise. The two lines that stop this (stop-and-diagnose and stop-after-three) are both paused, so nothing broke the chain. The person running Athena did not close the requests by hand and reported it for the steward.
cause: Athena treats a cause named in a request or a failure review as fact. Nothing requires the cause to be shown in the job records before a fix job is queued. A rejected fix job feeds the failure review, which writes the next request from the same unverified story. The stop-and-diagnose and stop-after-three rules are paused, so no counter on repeated rejections of one topic halts the chain or forces a diagnosis.
prevention: Add a check in the queueing path, covering both the failure review and hand-filed fix requests. Before a fix request is queued, it must cite the record that shows the cause: a check output, a verifier finding or a diff line. It must also be compared against the repo, so a fix for something already done is refused. Add a topic counter. After two rejections on one topic, the check refuses new fix requests on it and holds them for one diagnosis job whose only output is the verified cause. Turn the paused stop-after-three rule back on with this counter as its trigger.
proposed_request: Stop fix requests built on unverified causes. (1) When the failure review or a person queues a fix request after a rejection, require the request to cite the record that shows the cause (a failed check's output, a verifier finding, or a file and line in the current snapshot). Refuse the request, with a stated reason, if no such record is cited, if the cited record contradicts the claim, or if the repo already contains the fix. (2) Count rejected jobs per topic (same cited jobs or same deliverable files). After two rejections on one topic, refuse further fix requests on it and queue a single diagnosis job whose only deliverable is the verified cause with its evidence. Acceptance: replaying the five rejected jobs from 10 Nov 12:00 UTC (the acceptance-point check twice, show cited jobs' files to the reader, resolve every cited job to its reading, print deliverable counts for carried jobs) makes the check refuse or divert the last three, and a request that cites a real record still passes.
